text:
[NCBK.2.6] **Per-firing ordering.** Within one rule firing the seq order is:

```
RULE_LHS_FACTS   (if the firing matched ≥ 1 fact)
RULE_FIRE_BEGIN
  FACT_ASSERT      (if the RHS asserts)
  ACTION_<verb>    (per RHS action, after its primary effect)
  FACT_RETRACT     (if the RHS retracts)
RULE_FIRE_END
TIMER_ARMED      (if the rate gate admitted a `cooldown` rule's firing)
```

**`TIMER_ARMED` follows the bracket.** For a
firing of a `cooldown` rule that the rate gate admits ([RDSC.4a.8.2.3]), the
engine **must** emit `TIMER_ARMED` immediately after `RULE_FIRE_END`, with no
intervening event. For a firing the gate suppresses it **must not** emit one:
the gate records only the firings it admits ([LCDB.3.2.1]), so a suppressed
firing arms no window ([NCBK.2.3]). A consumer joins the event to its firing
by `timetag` ([NCBK.2.12]). The event belongs to the rule-level cooldown alone:
the engine **must not** emit one for the gate of a `cooldown:` on a `call`
([LCRS.8.2]), whether it admits the call or not.

`RULE_LHS_FACTS` is conditional like the body events: a **factless firing** —
a rule with no positive fact pattern (e.g. a pure timer/tick rule), or a
firing whose matched facts don't resolve to a live working-memory fact — emits
no `RULE_LHS_FACTS`; the `RULE_FIRE_BEGIN` bracket still opens. When present it
is emitted **immediately before** `RULE_FIRE_BEGIN` with no intervening event
(the two are produced atomically), and carries the resolved matched facts (≤
one per LHS pattern). An activation withheld before the bracket (a fire guard
whose condition is not `true`, [RDSC.4a.8.2.2]) emits neither.

**An `after` body's firing is factless.** The
follow-up rule that runs it ([LTAC.3]) matches only the compiler's timer,
tick and capture facts, and none of them is on the stream. The capture holds a
copy of the values the body reads, not the parent's facts ([LTAC.3.5]), so the
follow-up matched no fact of the parent firing and emits no `RULE_LHS_FACTS`.

Cross-tier bridges gate on `ACTION_PUBLISH`, not `FACT_ASSERT`: a `publish`
asserts nothing here, and an `emit` is local-only ([NCBK.10]).

alloy.name: ncbk_2_6__begin_iff_end
alloy.note: A BEGIN has an END and an END a BEGIN, at most one of each, whatever the fire guard did: a withheld activation has neither, a gate-suppressed firing and a full firing both. The pairing a consumer reads; bounded at seven positions and events.

alloy.name: ncbk_2_6__end_closes_the_bracket
alloy.note: Every event of the firing but TIMER_ARMED precedes RULE_FIRE_END: END closes the bracket. Not 'END is the firing's last event', which TIMER_ARMED after it refutes for an admitted `cooldown` firing (the armed probe's instance). Bounded at seven positions and events.

alloy.name: ncbk_2_6__fact
alloy.note: A resolved live LHS fact the stream carries. The compiler's timer, tick and capture facts an `after` body's follow-up matches are live in working memory and not on the stream, so that firing resolves none of these and emits no RULE_LHS_FACTS: the clause's factless `after` body is an instance of `ncbk_2_6__lhs_iff_matched`, not an exception to it.

alloy.name: ncbk_2_6__firing
alloy.note: The firing a selected activation became, if it became one (`lone`): a withheld activation is no firing, RDSC.4a.8.2.2. Its matched facts are the activation's resolved facts.

alloy.name: ncbk_2_6__position
alloy.note: A position in the global seq order, the ordered carrier: the positions rather than the events, so that a withheld activation can leave the stream with no event at all.

alloy.name: ncbk_2_6__seq_order
alloy.note: Two events never share a position: the stream order.

alloy.name: ncbk_2_6__suppressed_arms_no_timer
alloy.note: 'For a firing the gate suppresses it must not emit one': the gate's `false` leaves no TIMER_ARMED. The fact's iff read backwards, a transcription. Bounded at seven positions and events.

alloy.name: ncbk_2_6__timer_armed
alloy.note: TIMER_ARMED follows the bracket: at most one, present exactly when the rate gate admitted the firing, and then immediately after RULE_FIRE_END. The model's stream is this one firing's events, so 'no intervening event' is drawn against them alone: an event from outside the firing is not in the model. The payload and the timetag join (NCBK.2.12) are not drawn. A call's `cooldown:` gate (LCRS.8.2) is not in the model; TIMER_ARMED answers to the rule's gate alone, which is that sentence's instance and no more.

alloy.name: ncbk_2_6__timer_armed_follows_end
alloy.note: When present, TIMER_ARMED is after RULE_FIRE_END with no event between: the fact's conjunct restated, a transcription. Within this one-firing model the no-intervening half is also a consequence of the frame, since every other event is before END. Bounded at seven positions and events.

alloy.name: ncbk_2_6__timer_armed_iff_admitted
alloy.note: TIMER_ARMED exists exactly when there is a firing, its rule carries `cooldown` (its guard has the rate gate, RLOW.4.6.1), and the gate admitted it. From TIMER_ARMED's rule and the gate's (RDSC.4a.8.2.3: a verdict exactly for a gated firing). So a withheld activation, a firing with no gate and a suppressed firing arm nothing. Bounded at seven positions and events.

alloy.name: ncbk_2_6__timer_armed_is_last
alloy.note: When present, every other event of the firing precedes TIMER_ARMED: from END closing the bracket and TIMER_ARMED right after END. Bounded at seven positions and events.
